releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.15
releasesInRange.body:
This release lets `pnpm-workspace.yaml` delegate settings to other files and config dependencies with `include`, adds `lockfile.integrityTarget: tar` and tar-registry support, accepts zstd-compressed registry responses, and honors `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` in `pnpm deploy` and `pnpm install`. It also rejects registry metadata that names a different package than the one requested and speeds up workspace installs and macOS file linking.

### Minor Changes

- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` can now delegate settings to other YAML files and to config dependencies through a new `include` field. Each source may define only the settings the root manifest delegates to it. Every setting has one owner. Commands that change settings write each one to the file that owns it. A relative path in an included file is relative to that file. See [Splitting Settings Across Files](https://pnpm.io/config-includes).

  A config dependency supplies its settings through the YAML file named in the `pnpm.config` field of its `package.json`. The new `bootConfig` setting sets the release-age and trust policy pnpm uses to install config dependencies and the pnpm version from `packageManager`.

- Added the `lockfile.integrityTarget` setting. With `integrityTarget: tar`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` pins the hash of every package's uncompressed tar, so the lockfile no longer changes when a registry recompresses its tarballs or serves them as tars. pnpm learns a version's tar hash from the store or by downloading it once. `pnpm audit signatures` ties the tar hash to the signed `.tgz` integrity.

  ```yaml title="pnpm-workspace.yaml"
  lockfile:
    integrityTarget: tar
  ```

- pnpm can now install from a registry that serves uncompressed tars with zstd or gzip content coding. `pnpm-lock.yaml` records the hash of each tar. Declare such a registry with `serverType: pnpr` in `registries` to keep tarball URLs out of the lockfile. See [Tar registries](https://pnpm.io/registries#tar-registries).

  pnpm now decodes the content coding of tarball downloads itself. It rejects a zstd response whose window is larger than 8 MiB.

  Added the `maxTarballUnpackedSize` setting. It caps the bytes the files of one package may unpack to, 4 GiB by default.

- Registry revisions now always pin the hash of the uncompressed tar, the original included. pnpm records an original selected through the revision protocol, for example with a `+r0` specifier, as `revision: 0` in the lockfile and fetches it from the registry's digest route. pnpm checks a revision's tar whether the registry sends it as a tar, gzip, or zstd. Revision metadata must list revision 0 and mark the selected revision. pnpm rejects incomplete revision metadata with `ERR_PNPM_MALFORMED_METADATA`.

- pnpm now accepts zstd-compressed responses. Registries that serve zstd send package metadata in fewer bytes than with gzip, most of all the full metadata that settings such as `minimumReleaseAge` and `trustPolicy` read.

- `pnpm deploy` and `pnpm install` now use the `

releasesInRange.name: pnpm 11.28.7
releasesInRange.body:
This release rejects registry metadata that names a different package than the one requested, applies `trustPolicy` to the pnpm version a project pins, and caps unpacked package size with `maxTarballUnpackedSize`. It also removes support for registry revisions, fixes `verifyDepsBeforeRun` after filtered installs, and finishes commands with their own exit code when a pipe reader exits early.

### Patch Changes

#### Security

* pnpm now fails with `ERR_PNPM_REGISTRY_NAME_MISMATCH` if a registry returns metadata for a package other than the one requested. Before, pnpm installed the package under the name in the metadata, so `allowBuilds` rules for the requested package did not apply to it.

* pnpm now applies `trustPolicy` to the pnpm version a project pins in `packageManager` or `devEngines.packageManager`. A pinned version whose trust evidence was downgraded fails the command before pnpm switches to it or records it in the lockfile [#16319](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16319).

* `minimumReleaseAgeExcludePrune` and `trustPolicyExcludePrune` now keep exclusions for resolved configuration dependencies and their transitive dependencies [#17142](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17142).

* Added the `maxTarballUnpackedSize` setting. `pnpm install` fails with `ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_TOO_LARGE` when the files of one package unpack to more than this many bytes, 4 GiB by default [pnpm/tasks#81](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/81).

#### Resolving dependencies

* Registry revisions are no longer supported. pnpm now fails with `ERR_PNPM_REGISTRY_REVISIONS_UNSUPPORTED` on registry metadata that selects a revision, on a `+rN` version specifier, and on a lockfile entry with a `revision` field. `pnpm update --patches` is removed.

* When `pnpm install` resolves a dependency again, it now reuses a version that the install already resolved for the same package, as a fresh install does. Before, it kept the version the lockfile pinned and added a second copy of the package. A locked version still stays when nothing else in the install prefers another version. To pin a transitive dependency on purpose, use `overrides` [#17084](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17084).

* When another workspace project adds a different version of a package, a project's auto-installed peer on that package now moves to the version a fresh install picks. It used to stay on its locked version while any other project still accepted that version [#17058](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17058).

* An optional peer that pnpm adds to a project now keeps the version the lockfile recorded for that project only while the dependency graph still holds it. Otherwise it follows its provider to a version the graph holds. Before, pnpm kept a higher version that only the lockfile held, which left two copies of the peer [#16443](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16443).

prs.title: perf: optimize pnpm install metadata through pnpr
prs.author: kairosci
prs.body:
Improves pnpr package metadata handling and tar streaming for [pnpm/tasks#178](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/178).

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Verified package metadata now includes accurate tarball file counts and unpacked sizes.
  - Registry resolution better supports abbreviated metadata for time-based resolution and trust checks.
  - Package metadata preserves publisher verification markers, bundled dependencies, and precise release timestamps.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Trust-policy checks more reliably detect downgrades and fetch complete metadata when required.
  - Offline and cached metadata verification is more resilient across supported registry types.
  - Tarball inspection consistently records build requirements, file counts, unpacked sizes, and integrity data.

prs.title: fix: hold link: workspace dependencies under dedicated lockfiles with injection
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/179
Follow-up to pnpm/pnpm#17150.

Under `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false` and `injectWorkspacePackages: true`, an injected workspace dependency (`workspace:*`) is copied into the dependent project during its own install, whereas a workspace dependency declared with the `link:` protocol remains a symlink whose target project still needs to be installed.

Previously, `verifyDepsBeforeRun` skipped walking all workspace dependency edges when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false && injectWorkspacePackages: true`, and in pnpm v11 `@pnpm/workspace.projects-graph` failed to resolve `link:` specs because `@pnpm/npm-package-arg` does not recognize the `link:` protocol.

This PR:
- In pnpm v12 (`pnpm-cli` and `pnpm-package-manager`), keeps walking `link:` workspace dependency edges under dedicated lockfiles with `injectWorkspacePackages: true`, while continuing to skip injected workspace dependencies.
- In pnpm v11 (`@pnpm/workspace.projects-graph`), normalizes `link:` prefixes to `file:` before passing specs to `npa.resolve` in `parseDependencySpec`, so `createProjectsGraph` records `link:` workspace dependencies as graph edges (fixing both `--filter=<project>...` and `selectProjectsToVerify` in `@pnpm/exec.commands`).

prs.author: rf-molsson
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm update --interactive` marked the row under the cursor only with the `❯` glyph. In a long dependency list that is easy to lose track of. The dependency list previously turned off the prompt's cyan highlight (`highlight_active: false`), because repainting the row cyan with a single outer wrap would hide the colors that show which part of each target version changed.

This PR highlights the active row in cyan while keeping the row's own foreground colors (such as the semver diff segment) by re-applying the cyan foreground after every embedded ANSI reset sequence (`\x1b[39m` or `\x1b[0m`).

Before (the cursor is on `uuid`):

```
 ○ react         19.0.0 ❯ 19.3.1    https://react.dev/
❯○ uuid           9.0.0 ❯ 14.0.3
 ○ ramda         0.29.0 ❯ 0.32.0
```

After: the active row is painted in cyan (`\x1b[36m`), with cyan restored right after the semver diff reset (`\x1b[39m`):

```
^[[36m❯○ uuid      9.0.0 ❯ ^[[31m14.0.3^[[39m^[[36m   https://...^[[39m
```

prs.author: KSXGitHub
prs.body:
## Summary

`directory_deps.rs` holds 393 lines of code against the 400 that `perfectionist::overly_long_file` allows. Every addition to the directory-dependency freshness check therefore has to be paid for elsewhere in the file, and the next one trips the lint.

The items in it are the three stages of one descent, each reached through a single entry point, plus the vocabulary all three share.

- **`importer_deps`** reads the specs an importer declares, decides which of them name a directory dependency at all, answers a `link:` spec on its own, and resolves the rest to their lockfile entries.
- **`package`** checks one directory package: the manifest the resolver would read for it, whether this scope has checked it already, and the peers its own dependencies shadow.
- **`children`** compares the children the resolver walks for a package with the ones its snapshot records, and recurses into `package` for a child that is itself a directory.

The module root keeps what the three share: `LocalDepContext`, the staleness error they raise, the test for a `file:` spec, and the directory set the spec comparisons resolve against.

| `directory_deps/package.rs` | new, 63 |

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17188.

Under `nodeLinker: hoisted`, an install that reaches the linker imports again every patched package already in place, and every package whose peer suffix names a patched peer. `package_is_reusable` excluded any reference containing `(patch_hash=`, so `react-dom@19.2.0(react@19.2.0(patch_hash=…))` was excluded although `react-dom` is not patched.

This PR removes the exclusion. prs.title: fix(deps-restorer): keep an explicit `copy` import for built packages
prs.author: bradzacher
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17195

pnpm 12 imports a package with `clone-or-copy` when a lifecycle script or a patch will still write to it. It does this even when `packageImportMethod` is `copy`. An explicit `copy` already gives the package private files, so this PR keeps it. Every other method still changes to `clone-or-copy`. pnpm 11 has the same rule since 11.28.0, so only v12 changes.

This is important on Windows. On ReFS and Dev Drives, a clone of a store file that pnpm wrote a short time before can have zeros in place of data ([microsoft/CopyOnWrite#12](https://github.com/microsoft/CopyOnWrite/issues/12)). Users who set `copy` to stop clones still got clones for packages with install scripts or patches.

Changes:

- `effective_import_method` keeps `copy`. Both linkers get the method through it.
- The test of the import method for built slots also checks `copy` with a mutable and an immutable source.
- The `packageImportMethod` docs say which packages pnpm imports with `clone-or-copy`.
- A `pacquet` patch changeset.

_Agent follow-up (Claude Code, claude-opus-5-5): rebased onto main, shortened the changeset and linked the issue, restructured the `method_for` doc comment, and renamed the test to `needs_build_slots_never_share_inodes_with_their_source`._

Tests: the `pnpm-deps-restorer` tests pass (661 passed, 5 ignored). Without the fix, the new assertions fail (`left: Clone`, `right: Copy`). Clippy with `--deny warnings` and the pinned rustfm

prs.title: fix(dedupe): ignore deprecation notices in dedupe --check
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm dedupe --check` failed with "The lockfile would be rewritten, but no dependency resolution would change" when the only difference was a `deprecated` notice the registry added after the lockfile was written. The result depended on how fresh the metadata cache was, so the same commit could pass locally and fail in CI.

pnpm v12 compares the lockfile text in `--check` on purpose, so that changes a run makes outside the resolution diff, such as config dependencies, still fail the check (`dedupe_check_detects_config_dependency_changes_when_root_is_unselected`). This PR keeps that gate. When the text differs, the check now passes only if the env document is unchanged, the old main document is in the form pnpm writes, and serializing it with the new `deprecated` notices reproduces the rewritten text byte for byte. A rewrite that also reformats the lockfile still fails (`manifest_creation::native_build_is_skipped_when_not_materializing`). The lockfile guard still restores the original file.

pnpm v11 gates `dedupe --check` on the resolution diff only (`dedupeDiffCheck`), so it is not affected and gets no change.

The new e2e test fails without the fix with the exact error from the issue.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17198

prs.title: fix(tarball): do not retry rejected archive entry paths
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

When a downloaded archive contains a rejected entry path (such as `package/../outside.txt`, an absolute path, or a lone `.` naming the archive root), `pnpm-tarball` previously wrapped a plain `String` inside `TarballError::ReadTarballEntries(io::Error)` and fell through to the default `_ => true` arm in `is_transient_error`, retrying the download twice and sleeping through the `10s + 60s` retry backoff even when the archive had already passed integrity verification. `TarballError::PathTraversal` for zip archives was similarly missing from the permanent-error arms, and on `IntegrityKind::Tar` / `IntegrityKind::ResourceOrTar` streaming extractions `finish_tar_of`'s skipped-hash `IncompleteTar` placeholder masked the underlying extraction error.

This PR:
- Introduces a typed `RejectedEntryPathError` for `clean_archive_entry_path` rejections (matching the `OversizedManifestError` pattern).
- Preserves the extraction error in `finish_resource` when `finish_tar_of` returns `IncompleteTar` only because extraction failed early.
- Classifies `RejectedEntryPathError` and `TarballError::PathTraversal` as non-transient in `is_transient_error`.

`pnpm` v11 (`pnpm11/`) is unaffected: `parseTarball.ts` normalizes `..` traversal segments via `normalizeTraversal` rather than throwing a tar entry error, and `binary-fetcher` does not wrap `extractZipToTarget` in a retry loop.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17205

Attach a typed RejectedEntryPathError to TarballErr

prs.title: fix(fs/linux): read the umask without writing it
prs.author: KSXGitHub
prs.body:
## Summary

`current_umask` set the process mask to `0` to learn what it was and put it back, as POSIX leaves no other way: `umask(2)` returns the value it replaced. That window is process-wide, so a file another thread created inside it was created unmasked, with wider permissions than the user asked for. An install under `umask 077` could leave a world-readable file behind.

The window was known and argued harmless, and the argument holds for what it reasoned about: an unmasked file carries no executable bit, matches no desired mode, and so is copied by the import tiers rather than linked. It says nothing about the file's permissions, which is the defect.

Linux has published the mask in the `Umask:` line of `/proc/self/status` since 4.7, so it is read from there first and the window never opens. A kernel without the line, a host without `procfs`, and every other Unix fall back to the syscall pair, which now has nothing at all between its two calls.

One read per process either way: the `LazyLock` that kept the import hot path from paying per file is unchanged.

Found while reorganizing the workspace's `unsafe` code in pnpm/pnpm#17216, and split out of it so it can be reviewed and ship on its own. That PR carries the same fix today; once this lands it will merge `main` and drop its copy along with this changeset.

## Summary

`sigaction` keeps the one-argument and three-argument handler forms in a union, and nothing but `SA_SIGINFO` in the flags says which one it holds. The install read only the handler address out of the disposition it replaced and dropped the flags, so the chained call went through `extern "C" fn(c_int)` whatever the handler had been installed as. A handler installed with `SA_SIGINFO` was then called with its `siginfo_t` and context arguments left to whatever the registers happened to hold, which is undefined rather than merely incomplete.

prs.title: fix(pnpr): run libsql auth operations on a pool of connections
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

A pnpr deployment with Turso as the auth backend started answering every login and every authenticated request with a 500, while the database itself was healthy. Restarting pnpr fixed it until the next time.

Cause: the libsql backend ran every operation on one shared connection. On a remote database that connection is a Hrana stream, and each response carries the baton for the stream's next request. An operation dropped while its request was in flight (a client disconnecting, the auth timeout) never received the new baton, so the connection kept the spent one. The server then refused every later request:

```text
Auth database error: Hrana: `api error: `status=400 Bad Request, body=Received a baton that has already been used``
```

Reproduced locally against `libsql-server`: 300 authenticated requests cut off after 20 ms break auth permanently. Idle time and 300 parallel requests that complete do not.

The shared stream also let concurrent operations run inside each other's transactions. A token issued during a registration transaction could be rolled back with it.

**Fix: a connection pool, as sqlx does for the PostgreSQL and MySQL backends.** An operation checks out a connection and runs alone on it. The connection goes back to the pool only after the operation succeeded outside a transaction. Any other connection is closed, and a later checkout opens a fresh one. Pooled connections keep their HTTP client, so reusing one costs no new TCP or TLS handshake.

## Summary

Follow-up to https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17237, which merged before these review fixes landed on it. Two corrections.

**Bound the pool by the auth deadline without cancelling writes.** Qodo flagged on 17237 that only reads ran under the auth timeout, so a write that never got an answer held its pool slot forever. Once every slot was held that way, every token lookup failed. My first fix put every operation under the deadline. CodeRabbit and Qodo then pointed out the problem with that: a write the database commits after the deadline gets reported as a timeout, so a caller can be told a token or user wasn't created when it was. The contract on `with_auth_timeout` already ruled that out.

The pool now has two entry points:

- `read` runs under the deadline end to end, as reads did before the pool. A cancelled read changes nothing, and its connection is discarded.

`touch_key` keeps the read deadline it always had, with a comment: a lost last-used timestamp is harmless.
